title: Secrets, Auth Security & Scanning — Quick Revision

sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Beyond Rails' built-in protections, production applications need a secrets management strategy, dependency scanning, and static analysis in CI. Rails encrypted credentials (rails credentials:edit) is the modern approach — encrypted with the master key, committed to the repo, different per environment. bundler-audit scans the Gemfile.lock against the Ruby Advisory Database for known CVEs. Brakeman is a static analysis tool that scans Rails code for common vulnerabilities — SQL injection risks, mass assignment issues, unverified redirects, and more. JWT security deserves its own treatment: the algorithm confusion attack (never accept alg: none), the difference between HS256 (shared secret) and RS256 (asymmetric), and why you must validate the audience and issuer claims. This page covers all three areas.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: secrets-management, bundler-audit-brakeman, jwt-security. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
